verses.original: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ ἱερεὺς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Houtos gar ho Melchisedek basileus Salēm hiereus tou Theou tou Hypsistou ho synantēsas Abraam hypostrephonti apo tēs kopēs tōn basileōn kai eulogēsas auton
verses.literal: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him
verses.literalPt: PORQUE este Melquisedeque, que era rei de Salém, sacerdote do Deus Altíssimo, e que saiu ao encontro de Abraão quando ele regressava da matança dos reis, e o abençoou;

verses.original: ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος Βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ Βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ ὅ ἐστιν Βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης
verses.transliteration: hō kai dekatēn apo pantōn emerisen Abraam prōton men hermēneuomenos Basileus dikaiosynēs epeita de kai Basileus Salēm ho estin Basileus eirēnēs
verses.literal: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything First his name means king of righteousness Then also king of Salem means king of peace
verses.literalPt: A quem também Abraão deu o dízimo de tudo, e primeiramente é, por interpretação, rei de justiça, e depois também rei de Salém, que é rei de paz;

verses.original: ἀπάτωρ ἀμήτωρ ἀγενεαλόγητος μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές
verses.transliteration: apatōr amētōr agenealogētos mēte archēn hēmerōn mēte zōēs telos echōn aphōmoiōmenos de tō Huiō tou Theou menei hiereus eis to diēnekes
verses.literal: Without father or mother or genealogy without . . . beginning of days or end of life like the Son of God he remains a priest for all time
verses.literalPt: Sem pai, sem mãe, sem genealogia, não tendo princípio de dias nem fim de vida, mas sendo feito semelhante ao Filho de Deus, permanece sacerdote para sempre.

verses.original: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης
verses.transliteration: Theōreite de pēlikos houtos hō kai dekatēn Abraam edōken ek tōn akrothiniōn ho patriarchēs
verses.literal: Consider how great Melchizedek was Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder
verses.literalPt: Considerai, pois, quão grande era este, a quem até o patriarca Abraão deu os dízimos dos despojos.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ
verses.transliteration: kai hoi men ek tōn huiōn Leui tēn hierateian lambanontes entolēn echousin apodekatoun ton laon kata ton nomon tout’ estin tous adelphous autōn kaiper exelēlythotas ek tēs osphyos Abraam
verses.literal: Now . . . the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people that is from their brothers though they too are descended from . . . . . . Abraham
verses.literalPt: E os que dentre os filhos de Levi recebem o sacerdócio têm ordem, segundo a lei, de tomar o dízimo do povo, isto é, de seus irmãos, ainda que tenham saído dos lombos de Abraão.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν Ἀβραάμ καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν
verses.transliteration: ho de mē genealogoumenos ex autōn dedekatōken Abraam kai ton echonta tas epangelias eulogēken
verses.literal: But Melchizedek who did not trace his descent from Levi collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises
verses.literalPt: Mas aquele, cuja genealogia não é contada entre eles, tomou dízimos de Abraão, e abençoou o que tinha as promessas.

verses.original: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται
verses.transliteration: chōris de pasēs antilogias to elatton hypo tou kreittonos eulogeitai
verses.literal: And indisputably the lesser is blessed by the greater
verses.literalPt: Ora, sem contradição alguma, o menor é abençoado pelo maior.

verses.original: Καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ
verses.transliteration: Kai hōde men dekatas apothnēskontes anthrōpoi lambanousin ekei de martyroumenos hoti zē
verses.literal: In the case of the Levites mortal men collect the tenth but in the case of Melchizedek it is affirmed that he lives on
verses.literalPt: E aqui certamente tomam dízimos homens que morrem; ali, porém, aquele de quem se testifica que vive.

verses.original: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν δι’ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευὶ ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται
verses.transliteration: kai hōs epos eipein di’ Abraam kai Leui ho dekatas lambanōn dedekatōtai
verses.literal: And so to speak Levi who collects the tenth paid the tenth through Abraham
verses.literalPt: E, por assim dizer, por meio de Abraão, até Levi, que recebe dízimos, pagou dízimos.

verses.original: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ Μελχισέδεκ
verses.transliteration: eti gar en tē osphui tou patros ēn hote synēntēsen autō Melchisedek
verses.literal: For when Melchizedek met Abraham Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor
verses.literalPt: Porque ainda ele estava nos lombos de seu pai quando Melquisedeque lhe saiu ao encontro.

verses.original: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς νενομοθέτηται τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι
verses.transliteration: Ei men oun teleiōsis dia tēs Leuitikēs hierōsynēs ēn ho laos gar ep’ autēs nenomothetētai tis eti chreia kata tēn taxin Melchisedek heteron anistasthai hierea kai ou kata tēn taxin Aarōn legesthai
verses.literal: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood ( for on this basis the people received the law why was there still need for another priest to appear one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron
verses.literalPt: De sorte que, se a perfeição fosse pelo sacerdócio levítico (porque sob ele o povo recebeu a lei), que necessidade havia logo de que outro sacerdote se levantasse, segundo a ordem de Melquisedeque, e não fosse chamado segundo a ordem de Arão?

verses.original: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται
verses.transliteration: metatithemenēs gar tēs hierōsynēs ex anankēs kai nomou metathesis ginetai
verses.literal: For when the priesthood is changed the law must be changed . . . as well
verses.literalPt: Porque, mudando-se o sacerdócio, necessariamente se faz também mudança da lei.

verses.original: Ἐφ’ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν ἀφ’ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ
verses.transliteration: Eph’ hon gar legetai tauta phylēs heteras meteschēken aph’ hēs oudeis proseschēken tō thysiastēriō
verses.literal: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe from which no one has ever served at the altar
verses.literalPt: Porque aquele de quem estas coisas se dizem pertence a outra tribo, da qual ninguém serviu ao altar,

verses.original: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν εἰς ἣν φυλὴν περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν
verses.transliteration: prodēlon gar hoti ex Iouda anatetalken ho Kyrios hēmōn eis hēn phylēn peri hiereōn ouden Mōusēs elalēsen
verses.literal: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests
verses.literalPt: Visto ser manifesto que nosso Senhor procedeu de Judá, e concernente a essa tribo nunca Moisés falou de sacerdócio.

verses.original: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος
verses.transliteration: Kai perissoteron eti katadēlon estin ei kata tēn homoiotēta Melchisedek anistatai hiereus heteros
verses.literal: And this point is even more clear if another priest - like Melchizedek appears
verses.literalPt: E muito mais manifesto é ainda, se à semelhança de Melquisedeque se levantar outro sacerdote,

verses.original: ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου
verses.transliteration: hos ou kata nomon entolēs sarkinēs gegonen alla kata dynamin zōēs akatalytou
verses.literal: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession . . . but by the power of an indestructible life
verses.literalPt: Que não foi feito segundo a lei do mandamento carnal, mas segundo a virtude da vida incorruptível.

verses.original: μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ
verses.transliteration: martyreitai gar hoti Sy hiereus eis ton aiōna kata tēn taxin Melchisedek
verses.literal: For it is testified You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek
verses.literalPt: Porque dele assim se testifica: Tu és sacerdote eternamente, Segundo a ordem de Melquisedeque.

verses.original: Ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές
verses.transliteration: Athetēsis men gar ginetai proagousēs entolēs dia to autēs asthenes kai anōpheles
verses.literal: So . . . the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless
verses.literalPt: Porque o precedente mandamento é ab-rogado por causa da sua fraqueza e inutilidade

verses.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος δι’ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: ouden gar eteleiōsen ho nomos epeisagōgē de kreittonos elpidos di’ hēs engizomen tō Theō
verses.literal: ( for the law made nothing perfect . . . and a better hope is introduced by which we draw near to God
verses.literalPt: (Pois a lei nenhuma coisa aperfeiçoou) e desta sorte é introduzida uma melhor esperança, pela qual chegamos a Deus.

verses.original: Καὶ καθ’ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες
verses.transliteration: Kai kath’ hoson ou chōris horkōmosias hoi men gar chōris horkōmosias eisin hiereis gegonotes
verses.literal: And . . . none of this happened without an oath For others became priests without an oath
verses.literalPt: E visto como não é sem prestar juramento (porque certamente aqueles, sem juramento, foram feitos sacerdotes,

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν Ὤμοσεν Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα
verses.transliteration: ho de meta horkōmosias dia tou legontos pros auton Ōmosen Kyrios kai ou metamelēthēsetai Sy hiereus eis ton aiōna
verses.literal: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind You are a priest forever
verses.literalPt: Mas este com juramento por aquele que lhe disse: Jurou o Senhor, e não se arrependerá; Tu és sacerdote eternamente, Segundo a ordem de Melquisedeque),

verses.original: Κατὰ τοσοῦτο καὶ κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς
verses.transliteration: Kata tosouto kai kreittonos diathēkēs gegonen engyos Iēsous
verses.literal: Because of this oath Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant
verses.literalPt: De tanto melhor aliança Jesus foi feito fiador.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi men pleiones eisin gegonotes hiereis dia to thanatō kōlyesthai paramenein
verses.literal: Now . . . there have been many other priests since death prevented them from continuing in office
verses.literalPt: E, na verdade, aqueles foram feitos sacerdotes em grande número, porque pela morte foram impedidos de permanecer,

verses.original: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην
verses.transliteration: ho de dia to menein auton eis ton aiōna aparabaton echei tēn hierōsynēn
verses.literal: But because Jesus lives forever He has a permanent priesthood
verses.literalPt: Mas este, porque permanece eternamente, tem um sacerdócio perpétuo.

verses.original: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους δι’ αὐτοῦ τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: hothen kai sōzein eis to panteles dynatai tous proserchomenous di’ autou tō Theō pantote zōn eis to entynchanein hyper autōn
verses.literal: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him since He always lives - to intercede for them
verses.literalPt: Portanto, pode também salvar perfeitamente os que por ele se chegam a Deus, vivendo sempre para interceder por eles.

verses.original: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς ὅσιος ἄκακος ἀμίαντος κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος
verses.transliteration: Toioutos gar hēmin kai eprepen archiereus hosios akakos amiantos kechōrismenos apo tōn hamartōlōn kai hypsēloteros tōn ouranōn genomenos
verses.literal: Such a high priest truly befits us One who is holy innocent undefiled set apart from sinners and exalted above the heavens
verses.literalPt: Porque nos convinha tal sumo sacerdote, santo, inocente, imaculado, separado dos pecadores, e feito mais sublime do que os céus;

verses.original: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας
verses.transliteration: hos ouk echei kath’ hēmeran anankēn hōsper hoi archiereis proteron hyper tōn idiōn hamartiōn thysias anapherein epeita tōn tou laou touto gar epoiēsen ephapax heauton anenenkas
verses.literal: Unlike the other high priests He does not need to offer daily sacrifices first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people He sacrificed for sin . . . once for all when He offered up Himself
verses.literalPt: Que não necessitasse, como os sumos sacerdotes, de oferecer cada dia sacrifícios, primeiramente por seus próprios pecados, e depois pelos do povo; porque isto fez ele, uma vez, oferecendo-se a si mesmo.

verses.original: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον Υἱόν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον
verses.transliteration: ho nomos gar anthrōpous kathistēsin archiereis echontas astheneian ho logos de tēs horkōmosias tēs meta ton nomon Huion eis ton aiōna teteleiōmenon
verses.literal: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak but the oath which came after the law appointed the Son who has been made perfect forever
verses.literalPt: Porque a lei constitui sumos sacerdotes a homens fracos, mas a palavra do juramento, que veio depois da lei, constitui ao Filho, perfeito para sempre.
